clue.text: Not a true rock plant

parts.note: something not true is a sham, a fake
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener dismisses a so-called rock plant as an impostor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock plant' reads as one horticultural term, but 'plant' alone is the definition. The shamrock is the clover-like emblem of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The shamrock is a small clover, a living green thing that grows in soil.

clue.text: Save a bit — a single note

parts.note: a scrap is a small piece or bit
E is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: Someone hoards a little money while jotting down one musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrape, as in scrimp and scrape, is to economise by putting money aside bit by bit.

clue.text: Set about a fool and sicken following

indicators.note: the word for sicken comes after, following, the word for a fool

parts.note: an ass is a fool
to ail is to be ill, to sicken

explanation.surface: Attacking an idiot and then feeling ill afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To set about someone is to attack them, and to assail is to attack.

clue.text: Limits the area where cattle can graze

definitions.text: the area where cattle can graze

explanation.surface: Grazing boundaries are set for a herd.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is the extent or limits of something; it is also open grazing land for livestock, as on a ranch.

clue.text: Capacity to satisfy

explanation.surface: A container's volume is said to be enough to please.
explanation.definitionFit: Content is the amount a vessel holds, its capacity; as a verb it means to please or make happy.

clue.text: Ribald drunk at a wedding

indicators.note: a drunk person is all over the place, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

explanation.surface: A bawdy guest gets tipsy at a marriage reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges RIBALD into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridal is an adjective for things belonging to a bride or her marriage ceremony.

clue.text: Artist cheers wildly about love — fast creature!

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the letter for love
wildly tells us to throw the letters of the word cheers into disorder

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A painter cheers ecstatically about his love for a speedy animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' makes CEHRSE from CHEERS, and 'about' puts O inside it to give CEHORSE after RA.
explanation.definitionFit: A racehorse is a thoroughbred bred to run at speed, so a swift animal.

clue.text: Small daughter going out to get home

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
welling is flowing or going out, as water wells up from a spring

explanation.surface: A young girl leaves the house to get back home.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling is a house or residence where one lives.

clue.text: Capital fellow, putting pounds on, finished right

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from the Latin libra
taken as written
done means finished

explanation.surface: A man gains weight and is told he is completely correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting' joins the pounds to 'on'. 'Capital' looks like praise, as in 'a capital fellow', but means a man from the capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from London, the UK's capital city, is a native of that capital.

clue.text: Ringing soldier-boy and social-worker

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, soldiers in the British Army
a son is a boy
an ant is a worker among social insects

explanation.surface: A phone call comes from a young army man and a council welfare officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social-worker' suggests a council employee, but here it is an ant, the worker of a social insect colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A resonant sound is one that rings or echoes deeply.

clue.text: Those wanting a look-in need such protection

definitions.text: Those wanting a look-in need such protection

parts.words: Those wanting a look-in need such protection
parts.note: a look-in suggests a chance to take part, but it is also looking in through a monitor or TV, and the word also means a shield

explanation.surface: Outsiders hoping for a chance need cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen is both a protective barrier and the display surface one looks into on a television.

clue.text: Second-hand, but found serviceable?

explanation.surface: An item bought pre-owned turned out to be useful after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Used describes goods that have had a previous owner; it also means put to work or employed.

clue.text: Soft grain cheaper, which is much appreciated

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for soft
rice is a cereal grain
something cheaper costs less

explanation.surface: Gentle rice at a lower price is welcomed by shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which is' is a link. The definition's sense is invaluable, far beyond any price.
explanation.definitionFit: Something priceless is beyond value, so highly treasured.

clue.text: Call everybody into the house

indicators.note: into means the word for everybody goes inside the letters for house

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
all means everybody

explanation.surface: Summoning the whole family indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts ALL inside HO.
explanation.definitionFit: A hallo is a shout or greeting used to attract attention.

clue.text: Left a good man to carry on

parts.note: ST is saint, a good man

explanation.surface: A virtuous man was abandoned to keep going alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to continue or endure over time.

clue.text: A mean club may be forced to provide such transport

indicators.note: forced suggests the letters are pushed out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: A stingy sports club is made to lay on an emergency vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be forced' rearranges A MEAN CLUB; 'to provide' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambulance is a vehicle carrying the sick or injured to hospital.

clue.text: Upset and quite possibly enraged

indicators.note: quite possibly signals the letters of enraged could form another word

explanation.surface: Someone is upset and probably furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite possibly' rearranges ENRAGED.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to throw into disorder or disturb.

clue.text: Quicker to give a reminder?

explanation.surface: Someone is quick off the mark to nudge your memory.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is the theatre prompter, the person who gives actors forgotten lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompter is the comparative of prompt, meaning faster; a prompter is also someone who feeds cues to performers.

clue.text: Complains, though not against checks being made

parts.note: pro means for, not against
tests are checks

explanation.surface: Grumbles, though in favour of inspections taking place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being made' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who protests objects, voicing disapproval.

clue.text: An excellent little savoury food!

parts.note: rare can mean unusually good, excellent
a bit is a little

explanation.surface: Praising a fine small snack.
explanation.walkthrough: RAREBIT, or Welsh rarebit, is a British dish of melted cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is a cheese-on-toast dish, a savoury snack.

clue.text: It's time to question this work

parts.note: to ask is to question

explanation.surface: A boss says it is high time to query this job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' and 'this' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work or a job to be done.

clue.text: Bearing with average sound

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for average is heard rather than written

parts.note: the mean is an average

explanation.surface: Someone's demeanour comes with an ordinary tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' turns MEAN into its sound-alike, spelt MIEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's look or demeanour, their bearing.

clue.text: Game not to be played with electrical equipment

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are moved around in play to form a new word

explanation.surface: A game not meant for toying with electrical gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be played' rearranges GAME NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A magneto is a small generator producing current, as for ignition in engines.

clue.text: Restore material, then display

indicators.note: then means the word for display comes after the word for material

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric, a material
to air is to show or display, as in airing views

explanation.surface: Mend the cloth and then show it off.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair is to fix or mend something back to working order.

clue.text: An explosion due to the cold?

definitions.text: An explosion due to the cold?

parts.words: An explosion due to the cold?
parts.note: explosion suggests a blast or bomb, but here it is a sudden burst from the nose of someone with a cold

explanation.surface: A blast caused by freezing weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneeze is a sudden involuntary expulsion of air, common with a head cold.

clue.text: Many delayed backing copper maybe

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, many

indicators.note: backing means the word for delayed is read in reverse

parts.note: late means delayed

explanation.surface: Lots of late support for a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns LATE into ETAL, after M. 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is one example of an element in that class, like iron or tin.

clue.text: Dull colour for the prudent environmentalist

parts.note: sage means wise or prudent
a Green is an environmental campaigner

explanation.surface: A wise ecologist chooses a muted shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage green is a soft greyish green, a subdued shade.

clue.text: American president's award

explanation.surface: A US leader's prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 's' is a link. Ulysses S. Grant was the eighteenth US president.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses S. Grant led the United States after the Civil War; a grant is also a sum of money awarded.

clue.text: The drink in prospect is a new one

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A fresh beverage is on the horizon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is a link. The answer runs through 'prospecT IS A NEw'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is a herbal tea, an infusion to drink.

clue.text: A mere lad having the makings of a poet

indicators.note: makings suggests raw material that can be reassembled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mere boy shows promise as a writer of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having the makings of' rearranges A MERE LAD. Walter de la Mare was an English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter de la Mare was an English writer of verse and children's stories.

clue.text: Spots redhead and remains

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word red

parts.note: ashes are the remains after burning

explanation.surface: A ginger-haired person has blemishes and leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redhead' reads as a ginger-haired person, but is the head of 'red'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash is an outbreak of red spots on the skin.

clue.text: Dreamy music that's just no go in church

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in means the word for go sits inside the letters for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a turn is a go, as in taking turns

explanation.surface: A piece of music that forbids any movement in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's just' is a link; 'in' puts TURN inside CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturne is a romantic piano piece evoking the night.
